scenes.headline: How an agent starts tool calls before its code finishes
scenes.sub: Speculative programmatic tool calling: running a half-written REPL cell.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Iris! When an agent acts by writing code, its tool calls wait for the whole cell. Here's how sPTC starts them while the code is still streaming.

scenes.text: Parse the cell as it streams, and pre-launch every tool call that is already fully specified. The finished cell collects a cached result.
scenes.say: The idea: parse the cell as it streams, and pre-launch any tool call that's already fully specified. The finished cell just collects the result.

scenes.title: Where a turn's time goes
scenes.say: Take one turn of a code-writing agent.

parts.note: the model streams its code cell

parts.say: then four eight-second sub-calls in a row, though the first was written twelve seconds in.

parts.note: sixty-two seconds, though the calls could run under the stream
parts.say: Sixty-two seconds, when the calls could have run underneath the stream, and alongside each other.

steps.say: As the model streams, a deepcopy fork of the REPL re-runs the partial program in a shadow namespace.
Any speculatable, pure call it can fully specify is launched right away, and registers a promise.

steps.note: a value from open() taints every call downstream of it
steps.say: Anything touching outside state, like opening a file, isn't evaluated, and calls that depend on it aren't speculated.
When the cell is done, the fork is thrown away and the real REPL runs it clean. Each call checks the store, and collects its result.

scenes.label: measured speed-up with RLM on OOLONG, five runs per cell
scenes.note: trajectory variance swamps a 15% scheduling gain
scenes.say: End to end, it measured one to one point two times faster, and that's hard to pin down: the agent chooses different work every run.

scenes.text: Once actions are programs, the harness is a runtime, and runtimes know how to overlap slow calls with fast ones.
scenes.say: Once actions are programs, the harness is a runtime, and runtimes know how to overlap slow calls with fast ones.

recap: A shadow fork runs the half-written cell
Pure, fully specified calls launch early
The real cell collects results from a promise store
scenes.say: To recap: a shadow fork runs ahead, safe calls launch early, and the real cell collects.
